item.title: Wiz Khalifa Returns To Warner With Two More Diamond Records
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Wiz Khalifa's team announced 12 new RIAA honors as the rapper reunites with Marsha St. Hubert through his 10K Projects deal.
item.content:encoded:
Wiz Khalifa has two more Diamond records to celebrate as he returns to the Warner Music Group family through 10K Projects.

His team announced 12 new RIAA certifications, led by Diamond honors for “Black and Yellow” and “Young, Wild, & Free” with Snoop Dogg. The same announcement puts “See You Again,” featuring Charlie Puth, at 16-times Platinum.

The list reaches back to his first major-label album, Rolling Papers, which arrived in 2011. “Black and Yellow,” “Roll Up” and “No Sleep” were all part of that breakthrough and now appear together in his team’s certification update.

Other hits also got upgrades. “Sucker for Pain,” with Lil Wayne and Imagine Dragons, reached six-times Platinum. “Work Hard, Play Hard” and “Roll Up” are now four-times Platinum. “No Sleep” reached three-times Platinum.

“Hopeless Romantic,” featuring Swae Lee, reached double Platinum. The Platinum list also includes two albums: Rolling Papers 2 and Mac & Devin Go To High School, his joint project with Snoop. “Bake Sale” and “FR FR,” featuring Lil Skies, reached the same level.

Earlier this month, Khalifa appeared in an Inked cover interview. That conversation predates this announcement.

The career milestones come as a label reunion is already underway. The release confirms his previously announced signing with 10K Projects and a return to working with Marsha St. Hubert, his former project manager and now the label’s president.

“It’s good to be home!” Khalifa said in the signing announcement.

His Warner ties go back to a brief Warner Records deal at 18. His team says he signed with Atlantic Records at 22. The move pairs him again with an executive who worked with him during that earlier chapter.

“I’m excited to welcome Wiz back home to WMG as we reunite to embark on a new era together at 10K Projects,” St. Hubert said. “From day one, Wiz has not only been one of the most innovative and talented artists I’ve ever worked with but one of the most stand up guys you can meet.”

The announcement does not disclose the deal’s value, length or ownership terms.

item.title: Clayface Review: A Dark, Disturbing And Refreshing Twist On The Superhero Genre
item.dc:creator: Chris L. Boogie Brown
item.description: DC Studios takes a terrifying turn with Clayface, a gruesome body-horror thriller that transforms a classic Batman villain into the centerpiece of a dark and surprisingly compelling tragedy.
item.content:encoded:
Clayface is the latest film from DC Studios, directed by James Watkins and co-written by Mike Flanagan and Hossein Amini. Based on one of the more recognizable villains from the world of Batman comics, the film stars Tom Rhys Harries, Naomi Ackie, Max Minghella, David Dencik, Joshua James, Nancy Carroll and more.

Clayface tells the story of Matt Hagen (Tom Rhys Harries), a rising Hollywood actor whose life and career take a devastating turn after a violent encounter leaves him severely disfigured. Desperate to restore his appearance, reclaim his identity and regain control of his life, Matt turns to an experimental medical treatment that comes with some truly horrifying consequences. What follows is a bleak and disturbingly tragic story of desperation, obsession, love, vengeance and the gradual loss of one’s humanity.

Clayface takes a much different approach from the two previous films released by DC Studios. Rather than focusing on superheroes saving the day, the film explores a darker corner of the DC Universe through a story firmly rooted in horror. In fact, aside from the numerous references to Gotham, casual moviegoers unfamiliar with the character could easily mistake Clayface for an original horror film rather than a DC Comics adaptation.

The film explores how Matt Hagen’s pursuit of fame, fortune, respect and revenge leads him down an increasingly destructive path. While this DC villain-centered feature may not reach the same cinematic heights as 2019’s Joker, I nevertheless found it entertaining throughout its runtime!

Director James Watkins effectively establishes an eerie atmosphere that gradually builds toward full-blown horror. While watching Clayface, I found myself reminded of two older films from a similar narrative wheelhouse: 1986’s The Fly and 1990’s Darkman. Although these are distinctly different films with their own unique stories, all three blend horrifying physical transformations with tragic characters and themes of revenge.

To me, there is something refreshing about seeing a comic book property embrace this kind of old-school horror sensibility rather than relying on the familiar superhero formula. Even though the dialogue occasionally falters and the pacing is uneven in spots, Watkins’ interesting direction and bold vision help overcome the film’s shortcomings.

As far as the performances are concerned, Tom Rhys Harries is excellent in the lead role of Matt Hagen. He is particularly effective at conveying the character’s physical and emotional deterioration. His intense, often stoic performance adds a tragic and deeply human dimension to the character, grounding the film’s more outrageous horror elements.

In a supporting role, Naomi Ackie also delivers a strong performance as Caitlyn Corr, the scientist whose involvement in Matt’s experimental treatment becomes increasingly central to the story. While the rest of the cast does an adequate job of rounding out the film’s narrative, several supporting characters are essentially generic villain types who receive relatively little screen time or development.

In terms of the visual horror on display, Clayface makes a strong impression through its effective combination of practical and visual effects. The grotesque transformations and graphic imagery give the film a visceral edge, making its R rating feel well-earned. The body horror is particularly effective and disturbing whenever the movie fully embraces its gruesome nature. Throughout its runtime, the film delivers several unsettling and downright horrifying moments that fans of the genre should certainly appreciate. Overall, this film definitely isn’t for the squeamish!

Ultimately, I really enjoyed Clayface and look forward to seeing it again! However, it’s important to reiterate that this is not a traditional superhero film. Instead, Clayface is a body-horror and revenge tale that happens to be based on a DC Comics character.

While the film delivers plenty of horror-driven thrills, don’t go into it expecting the large-scale action or spectacle typically associated with comic book movies. I particularly appreciated the creative approach taken with this character, especially the decision not to transform him into a conventional antihero. Instead, Matt Hagen remains a true villain whose terrifying transformation grants him a range of clever and disturbing abilities.

That distinction is important because it allows the film to explore the character’s darker impulses without feeling obligated to make him heroic or particularly sympathetic. While its horror-driven identity may not appeal to everyone, I found the film to be a fun, entertaining and refreshing change of pace.

Overall, I believe Clayface is the best of the three films DC Studios has released so far. Its willingness to take creative risks, embrace a darker side of comic book storytelling and venture beyond the conventional superhero formula makes it well worth checking out!

Clayface is now playing in theaters everywhere and comes highly recommended, especially for fans of horror and darker comic book adaptations.

Enjoy!

item.title: Are Trump Cronies Picking On An 82-Year Old Senior Citizen?
item.dc:creator: Houston Williams
item.description: Virginia Senator Louise Lucas faces federal marijuana charges, but her history of challenging Confederate monuments and Donald Trump raises real questions about political retaliation.
item.content:encoded:
This not poll-tricks as usual.

Louise Lucas may be facing federal racketeering charges involving marijuana, but the arrest of the 82-year-old Virginia senator has ignited a much larger question about race, political retaliation and the price of opposing Donald Trump. Yup. Here we are.

The powerful Virginia Democrat, who has served in the state Senate since 1992, was indicted in connection with an alleged $4.5 million marijuana operation involving several relatives. Federal prosecutors claim she used her political influence to benefit the enterprise while pursuing legislation that could have enriched her family.

Those are serious allegations. However, Lucas has not been convicted, and her supporters are questioning whether the federal government has an entirely different agenda. By the way, her backers are scared that the government will come for them next, I am being told.

Lucas, a legend of many sorts, has been an outspoken critic of Trump and a supporter of the movement to remove Confederate monuments in Virginia. Remember that? During the racial justice demonstrations of 2020, she became a controversial figure in Portsmouth, where protesters targeted a Confederate monument. The confrontation eventually resulted in the destruction of portions of the monument. There were even criminal charges levied against Lucas at the time. They were all later dismissed.

So now, she catches a R.I.C.O.? The symbolism is impossible to ignore. A Black woman who challenged Confederate imagery and openly opposed Trump is now facing the possibility of spending her remaining years in federal prison. I do not see this as happenstance.

Coincidence? Political revenge? Or a legitimate criminal investigation? Tell me what you think in the comments.

Anyway, the indictment was unsealed less than two weeks before the midterm elections. Coincidence? I think not. Lucas had also championed an unsuccessful redistricting effort intended to strengthen Democratic representation in Congress. She put in the effort and the work though.

Virginia Governor Abigail Spanberger criticized the timing, suggesting it undermined public confidence in the Justice Department.

“I have read the charging document alleging a series of criminal acts by a member of the Virginia Senate. In our American system of justice, people are presumed innocent until proven guilty, and that is true for Senator L. Louise Lucas. She and her family deserve the opportunity to present their defense and speak to the allegations presented.

“The timing of this indictment undermines the U.S. Department of Justice’s previously longstanding policy of not taking legal actions — to include indictments or significant investigative steps — close to an election and sadly, this timing further erodes the trust the American people deserve to have in the Department of Justice.”

Meanwhile, Attorney General Todd Blanche rejected accusations of political retaliation, insisting, “We don’t do political paybacks.” We do not believe you, bro, you need more people.

Could prominent Democrats and other influential figures be reluctant to defend Lucas aggressively because they fear attracting the attention of Trump’s Justice Department themselves? That is what I am hearing.

Lucas insists she will not be intimidated. She has defeated them before and I think this 82-year old lioness will win again. We know that the political landscape is full of all sorts of criminality. And yet, much of it goes unchecked and overlooked. That is another article and my opinion.

America’s contentious struggle over race, power, justice and more is really feeling quite evil at t his point.

item.title: Aspen Kartier Thrown In Jail & Gets Strict No-Dogs Order Over Puppy Abuse
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Aspen Kartier received jail time and strict dog restrictions in the puppy abuse case sparked by her Twitch livestream.
item.content:encoded:
Aspen Kartier was sent to jail in her puppy abuse case, with a court order that also keeps her away from dogs.

The rapper, whose legal name is Aspen Easterling, received a one-year sentence: 10 days in jail and the rest on probation. She got credit for two days served, FOX 5 Atlanta reported, citing the DeKalb County Solicitor-General’s Office.

The judge denied her bid for first-offender status, so the conviction stays on her record. A second cruelty charge was dropped. Her probation bars her from owning or caring for dogs, or sharing a room with one. Random checks will enforce those terms.

She must take 24 anger management classes, finish an animal abuse prevention program and do 100 hours of community service. The court ordered her to pay LifeLine Animal Project $3,048 for the puppy’s care, plus $39 monthly probation fees.

The case began with her January 29 Twitch stream. PETA described a three-month-old puppy being hit and lifted by the skin of its back. The group later posted footage on Vimeo. The historical clip contains disturbing footage of animal abuse.

Viewers helped bring the case to police. PETA emergency response director Kristin Rickman told FOX 5 in February that dozens of people contacted the group about the stream.

“Within a few hours, we identified the suspect’s real name and physical address… we immediately shared that with Brookhaven Police.”

Brookhaven officers arrested Aspen Kartier on January 30 and removed the Maltipoo from her home. As AllHipHop reported at the time, police said the puppy appeared healthy when they found it. DeKalb County Animal Control took custody of the dog.

The stream also cost her access to Twitch. The platform suspended her account for breaking its rules. Early reports did not establish how long that ban would last.

In February, FOX 5 reported that animal services was holding the puppy as evidence. PETA honored Brookhaven police with its Compassionate Police Department Award for the rescue, crediting the officers for acting on the information it shared.

Aspen Kartier and another person who claimed to own the puppy gave up their rights to it.

item.title: Funkmaster Flex May Have Another Trick Up His Sleeve After MSG Chaos
item.dc:creator: illseed
item.description: Funkmaster Flex appears to be exploring legal options after his Madison Square Garden confrontation with TT Torrez's husband, but is the threat serious or strategic?
item.content:encoded:
Funkmaster Flex may have discovered a legal loophole in his increasingly contentious dispute with former Hot 97 colleague TT Torrez and her husband, Shadow Stokes. Or maybe he’s just having a little fun with the situation. Either way, the lawyers are circling.

Remember, this controversy erupted at Madison Square Garden during the New York Knicks’ season opener. Shadow allegedly pursued Flex aggressively inside the Delta lounge, prompting security personnel to intervene. Video footage captured the commotion, but the circumstances leading up to it remain disputed.

The confrontation stems from an earlier incident involving TT Torrez, who has accused Flex of violently shoving her. That’s a serious allegation, particularly considering their lengthy and reportedly strained history as former colleagues at Hot 97.

Now, Flex seems to be turning (trying at least) the legal conversation in another direction.

Flex has consulted legal counsel about his options following the MSG encounter and they made a joint post to double down. One hypothetical scenario involves whether he could have suffered an injury while retreating from Shadow’s alleged aggression.

If someone aggressively pursues you and you hurt yourself trying to escape, could that create grounds for a lawsuit? Apparently, that’s one of the questions being floated. Whether this holds up in court is another matter.

The lawyer appearing with Flex in a video who has indicated he’s ready to represent him. However, the attorney’s enthusiasm comes with an interesting caveat. His declaration in the comments included a laughing emoji. Hmmmm…always entertaining.

My interpretation? Flex might be sending a message without necessarily intending to file anything. He’s possibly mudding the narrative surrounding Torrez’s allegations. Maybe.

Of course, a hypothetical injury is not proof of an actual injury. So, there’s that. He’d have to prove that.

Meanwhile, Shadow has remained quiet since going ham defending his wife. And wife TT Torrez has not issued another statement since the initial press release.

Could this become an actual courtroom showdown? Perhaps. But I suspect we’re witnessing a little psychological chess disguised as legal strategy.

For now, everybody seems to be keeping their attorneys close and their next moves closer.

We’ll see.

item.title: North West Gets A “Baddies” Chain Offer After Going Full Natalie Nunn
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: North West dressed as Natalie Nunn for Halloween, and the reality star responded with an offer to send her a "Baddies" chain.
item.content:encoded:
North West, the eldest daughter of Kim Kardashian and Kanye West, went all in on her Natalie Nunn Halloween costume, and the reality star has now offered to upgrade one of its accessories.

Nunn promised the 13-year-old a “Baddies” chain after North dressed as her in a series of TikTok videos this week. The look included a prosthetic chin, a black bob and a version of the jewelry that tied the outfit to Nunn’s reality-TV franchise.

The videos drew millions of views, according to HOT97.

“I GOTTA GET @northwest her baddie chain now! SHE GETS A BADDIE CHAIN HAPPY HALLOWEEN MONTH !!” Nunn wrote, according to HOT97.

Hollywood Life reported that Nunn shared North’s TikTok on Instagram with her offer. Her response put a friendly finish on an imitation that went well beyond borrowing a hairstyle. North used the added chin to exaggerate one of Nunn’s most recognizable features, then built out the rest of the look around her.

The outfit paired a black Zeus Network tank top with a pleated black skirt, sheer socks and black-and-white sneakers. Bold makeup and dramatic lashes completed the transformation. The chain read “CEO Baddies,” making the reference clear even without the facial prosthetic.

Those details drew on two stages of Nunn’s television career. She first appeared on the fourth season of Oxygen’s “Bad Girls Club” in 2009 before becoming a central figure in “Baddies.” The newer franchise supplied both the network reference on North’s shirt and the name on her chain.

Nunn’s chin also had a Hip-Hop connection before this Halloween look. Nicki Minaj referenced it on Lil Uzi Vert’s 2023 song “Endless Fashion.” North’s costume brought the same recognizable feature to her version of the reality star without sacrificing the rest of Nunn’s style.

The dress-up ran in the family. A day before North’s reveal, Kim Kardashian chose her daughter as the model for her own Halloween look.

Kardashian wore a long teal wig, gothic-style makeup and face gems meant to resemble North’s dermal piercings. She also copied North’s pose, placing one hand over part of her face while wearing layered graphic clothing.

item.title: LeBron James Brushes Off Donald Trump’s Fury Over National Anthem Controversy
item.dc:creator: AllHipHop Staff
item.description: LeBron James brushed off Donald Trump's anthem criticism after the Cleveland game, adding a brief jab to their long-running feud.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump accused the Sixers star of disrespecting the country for stretching and making a shooting motion during the national anthem at Tuesday’s season opener against New York.

The president kept up the criticism during a Thursday rally in Sioux City, Iowa, treating the warm-up as a scandal.

“While listening to our National Anthem, LeBron James disrespects our Country! I said right from the beginning that he’s no good, a TOTAL DISGRACE. LeBron James should apologize to all of those Great American Warriors and Heroes who died for the American Flag, and all that our Country stands for!” a fuming President Trump wrote.

LeBron James answered Donald Trump’s demand for an apology with a laugh, brushing off the president’s criticism after Philadelphia’s game against Cleveland on Thursday, October 22.

“Must have been a slow news day at the office. Slow news day at the office,” James said.

Trump’s complaint focused on a clip from Tuesday’s pregame ceremony at Madison Square Garden that spread online Wednesday.

This is not the first time Trump has turned a question about James into a personal complaint. In July, the president was asked to choose between James and Michael Jordan during an Oval Office exchange with Fox News correspondent Peter Doocy.

Trump picked Jordan, whom he described as a friend and golf companion. He then suggested James might be racist, adding that James might simply dislike him. Trump supplied no evidence for the accusation, as AllHipHop reported at the time.

That clash came as James announced his move to the 76ers. It followed years of public conflict, including James’ criticism of Trump over the Golden State Warriors’ White House invitation in 2017. In 2018,

Trump attacked James’ intelligence after James interviewed him on CNN with Don Lemon. Jordan defended James.

James has also opposed Trump in presidential campaigns. In October 2024, he endorsed Kamala Harris with a video montage of Trump’s comments about immigrants and Black jobs. The montage also included comedian Tony Hinchcliffe’s watermelon joke at Trump’s Madison Square Garden rally.

James framed that endorsement around his children, his family and the future in which they would grow up. He urged voters to choose Harris.

“When I think about my kids and my family and how they will grow up, the choice is clear to me,” he wrote.

item.title: John Legend Explains How Pharrell Got Him To Talk On “Fireflies”
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: John Legend's "Fireflies" linked his work with Pharrell to themes of loss and resilience, with a video set around housing-project life.
item.content:encoded:
John Legend said Pharrell Williams pushed his “Fireflies” verses toward conversation rather than melody.

The Muse track was written by Pharrell, who also appeared on it. The song dealt with loss, inequality and resilience.

That subject matter carried into the Paul Hunter-directed video, released September 25. The video shows Legend at the piano with the Hollywood Cinematic Orchestra, alongside scenes of life in a housing project. It framed those scenes as a story of hardship and hope, tying the performance to the lives at the center of the song.

Legend contrasted his current creative freedom at Republic with Kanye West’s early oversight.

“I’m more of a free agent now and able to just do whatever I want musically,” he told the Associated Press.

The full-album partnership grew from a smaller job: Legend’s part on Clipse’s “The Birds Don’t Sing.” Pharrell heard that performance and proposed a project built around him.

Clipse returned for “Bodies On The Floor” on Muse. Apple Music’s album notes connect the track to “Taps,” the military tune, with a short introduction leading into the collaboration. The record’s range also takes in funk, gospel and Afrobeat.

Legend had described that mix as a way to carry earlier music forward. “My music has always been me channeling the ancestors, taking what they gave us and making something new,” he said in the label’s September release.

Legend also recalled Jay-Z telling him, “You’re our voice.”

Questions of freedom and control also run through his stage work. Legend wrote the score for “Imitation of Life,” with a book by Lynn Nottage and direction by Whitney White.

In a Howard University essay, co-producer Pat Parks described Delilah as the Black mother whose work helped build Bea Pullman’s business. Yet Bea, her White partner, became its public face and held more control.

“Her labor created value, but she did not have equal power to determine what that value became,” Parks wrote. Parks also connected that imbalance to Delilah’s daughter, Peola, who sought opportunities by passing as White.

The production begins performances at The Shed on November 21 and runs through January 3, 2027.

item.title: “Love & Hip Hop” Brings Its Stars Back To Face The Past
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Love & Hip Hop unveiled its farewell trailer, with new interviews and a November 10 premiere on VH1, BET and MTV.
item.content:encoded:
“Love & Hip Hop: The Final Chapter” rolled out a trailer ahead of its November 10 premiere on VH1, BET and MTV.

The six-part series will start at 8 P.M. ET. New episodes will then air Tuesdays at 8 P.M. ET on VH1.

Stevie J, Joseline Hernandez, Mimi Faust and Yandy Smith are among those giving new interviews. Rasheeda Frost, Trick Daddy, Trina, Ray J, Safaree Samuels, Scrappy and Yung Joc will also take part. Angela Yee, Nina Parker and Jess Hilarious will add their views alongside the cast.

The series will draw from all four cities: New York, Atlanta, Hollywood and Miami. Cast members will share the floor with producers, executives and journalists to look at the show’s place in music and TV.

That look back was the plan when VH1 first announced the project in May.

Instead of a new season in one city, the network promised to trace how stars rose through the ranks. It would look at the businesses they built and the disputes that kept their names in the news.

The franchise began in 2011, putting artists’ work and their personal lives on the same screen. Cardi B was one of the artists whose careers became part of the show’s story. She is not named in the new interview lineup.

For Lashan Browning, who founded the show’s production company, Antoinette Media, the farewell also includes the behind-the-scenes crews.

Antoinette Media also produced the franchise’s Atlanta and Miami shows. In May, she thanked the cast for sharing their lives and the producers who helped shape each story. She credited her team for their work through the seasons, as well as the fans who stayed with them.

“The ‘Love & Hip Hop’ franchise has always been about the people,” Browning said then. “Their dedication is why this franchise resonated for so many years.”

VH1’s May plan went beyond the TV episodes, too. After the debut, BET’s digital platform, BET Immersed, was set to feature the series on a digital cover. More images and a look behind the scenes were part of that plan.

item.title: Rick Ross Leaving Larry Jackson’s Gamma? Meeting With EMPIRE Boss Raises Questions
item.dc:creator: illseed
item.description: Rick Ross' meeting with EMPIRE founder Ghazi and recent social media changes have fueled rumors his partnership with Larry Jackson's gamma. may be over.
item.content:encoded:
Rick Ross may be preparing for another major business move, and the clues suggest his relationship with music executive Larry Jackson and gamma. could be coming to an end.

Rick Ross is moving on! Or at least that’s what it looks like, you guys.

A couple of years ago, Rick Ross entered into a major partnership with Larry Jackson and his company, gamma. Now, if you don’t know Larry Jackson, let me tell you something. This man is a kingmaker and a queenmaker in the music business. He’s been helping create stars, build brands and make people wealthy for decades.

And a lot of people don’t realize he’s also one of the key figures who helped bring Kanye West, now known as Ye, back into the mainstream music business. That relationship has been controversial, but Jackson helped put the infrastructure behind Ye’s latest comeback, including his album Bully and a return to major concert stages.

That’s no small accomplishment.

But anyway, that success was supposed to extend to other artists, and Rick Ross was one of them.

Back in September 2023, Ross and his Maybach Music Group announced a partnership with gamma. that was supposed to go well beyond traditional music releases. We’re talking multimedia projects, brand opportunities, podcasting and other ventures designed to push the Biggest Bawse into a new era.

Jackson had previously spoken highly of Ross, including his larger-than-life personality and ability to entertain people beyond music.

And let’s be clear, Rick Ross is hilarious. The man has turned his personality into a business all by itself.

But somewhere along the way, something may have gone awry.

Now, we don’t know exactly what happened, and nobody has publicly confirmed a breakup. However, the Internet detectives have started connecting some dots.

According to social media observations circulating online, Ross and Jackson no longer follow each other on Instagram. Ross also reportedly no longer follows gamma.

Now, we know that unfollowing somebody doesn’t automatically mean a business relationship is finished. But in today’s entertainment industry, social media activity can sometimes provide a BIG clue that something is happening behind the scenes.

And there’s another clue that’s much harder to ignore.

Rick Ross recently met with Ghazi, the founder of EMPIRE.

On October 21, Ross posted about their meeting on Instagram, describing the encounter as “Big Conversations!” and tagging Ghazi.

That’s significant.

As you already know, EMPIRE is one of the biggest independent music companies in the business. Ghazi has built an operation that competes with major labels while giving independent artists and established stars another way to release and monetize their music.

From an independent Hip-Hop perspective, EMPIRE is a monster.

So, when Rick Ross is publicly having big conversations with Ghazi while people are questioning his relationship with gamma., naturally, eyebrows are going to rise.

Does that mean Ross is leaving Larry Jackson? Not necessarily. Does it mean a new business arrangement could be developing? Absolutely.

There is also speculation that Ross’ recent legal situation could have something to do with a possible fracture in the relationship. I’m not necessarily buying that theory.

Ross has faced allegations stemming from a recent arrest, but those allegations are not proof of wrongdoing. The legal process has to play out, and we have no verified evidence connecting that situation to his business dealings with gamma.

Personally, I think there could be something else happening here.

Money. Business. Creative control. Expectations.

Those are the things that can make or break even the strongest partnerships in the music industry.

And remember, Rick Ross is not some new artist looking for somebody to put him on. He’s an established businessman with his own label, catalog, partnerships and a brand that reaches far beyond Hip-Hop.

That gives him options.

For now, we know Ross publicly connected with Ghazi. We also have reports of social media changes that suggest something could be happening with Jackson and gamma. What we don’t have is confirmation that the partnership has officially ended.

But I would definitely keep my eyes on this one.

Why This Potential Move Matters

There’s some important history here. Larry Jackson launched gamma. in 2023 with an ambitious model built around artist partnerships, technology, distribution and opportunities beyond recorded music. Rick Ross and Maybach Music Group were among the company’s early high-profile partners, alongside names associated with Snoop Dogg and Death Row Records. Meanwhile, Ghazi founded EMPIRE in 2010 and built it into a powerful independent music operation with a strong presence in Hip-Hop and an expanding international footprint. A potential Ross move would therefore represent more than a change in distribution. It could signal a new direction for one of Hip-Hop’s most recognizable entrepreneurial brands.

And that’s why I’m watching.

Because at the end of the day, money rules everything around these people. If there’s a real discrepancy in the relationship, we may find out soon enough.

What do you think? Is Rick Ross preparing to leave Larry Jackson and gamma. for EMPIRE, or are people reading too much into an Instagram post? Drop your thoughts in the comments.
